To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the chemical diffusion coefficient D in UO2 is a very strong function of oxygen potential, (ii) the diffusion mechanism is vacancy diffusion with a change to interstitial diffusion at high oxygen potential (iii) the diffusion coefficient in (U,Pu)O2 is very close to that in pure UO2 and the diffusion mechanism is the same.

1) The diffusion coefficient of the cations in UO2-(Pu,U)O2 decreases with increasing oxygen potential by more than 4 orders of magnitude, and 2) The diffusion mechanism in UO2 changes with oxygen potential, from interstitial mechanism at high oxygen potential to vacancy mechanism at lower oxygen potential.
the chemical diffusion coefficient in the solid solution (U, Pu )O2 is a strong function of the oxygen potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diffusion of metal atoms in UO2 and UO2-PuO2 solid solutions.
the diffusion and the solubility of plutonium in uranium dioxide.
the development of a model for the diffusion of metal atoms in UO2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D is very sensitive to the oxygen potential and that it decreases with increasing oxygen potential.
the chemical diffusion of the cations is strongly dependent on the oxygen potential and that this dependence is mainly due to the formation of oxygen vacancies.

the diffusion coefficient of UO2-(Pu,U)O2 decreases with increasing oxygen potential, and that the diffusion mechanism changes from vacancy mechanism to interstitial mechanism at a certain oxygen potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D depends strongly on ΔG(O2).
in UO2 and UO2-(Pu)O2, the diffusion of U and Pu is strongly dependent on ΔG(O2), but the diffusion mechanism does not change with ΔG(O2).
the diffusion coefficient is a function of the oxygen potential, and not of the oxygen content, as is usually assumed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion coefficient of the U and Pu atoms is strongly dependent upon the oxygen potential and the U/Pu-ratio.
the chemical diffusion coefficient in UO2 and UO2-PuO2 depends strongly on the oxygen partial pressure and the oxygen potential.
the chemical diffusion coefficient of metal atoms in UO2-(Pu,U)O2 is strongly dependent on the oxygen chemical potential.
